author: cli
text: RULE 1 IS TOO TIGHT, and its own docstring says so. The prose is right - 'a class or def inside a function body cannot be named from OUTSIDE that body' - but the code drops the target unconditionally: it walks dst_ent's parents, finds a function, and returns 'function-local' without ever asking where src_ent is. When the caller IS the enclosing function, the target is perfectly reachable, and that is the ordinary Python closure idiom. MEASURED 2026-08-16 under 0.55.2 against three real Python repos outside the corpus (psf/requests 8068356, pallets/click cbd7a41, Textualize/rich 9d8f9a3), ground truth from stdlib ast with real scope tracking: 60 true call edges dropped where the target is a def nested DIRECTLY inside the caller. rich alone loses 50, including rich.tree.Tree.__rich_console__ -> make_guide, which is its core render path and is called six times in that one function. Overall Python edge recall: requests 97%, rich 90%, click 68%. FIX: before returning 'function-local', check whether src_ent is the enclosing function or nested within it - if so the target is in scope and the edge is real. Cheap and unambiguous; a call from a function to a def it directly contains has exactly one candidate. DO NOT loosen rules 2 and 3 with it: the attribute-call rule is doing real work - 111 of the 184 misses in this measurement are receiver.method() calls that memway REFUSES to guess, which is correct behaviour and the whole point of the 23% fix. The oracle counts those as misses; they are not. This is the 'unfalsified in the too-tight direction' risk that has been on the open list since 0.54.3, now with a number and a reproduction.

author: cli
text: FIXED in 0.55.3 - supersedes the note below, which diagnosed it. Rule 1 now asks _in_scope(src_ent, encloser) before refusing: if the caller IS the enclosing function, or is nested within it, the target is lexically in scope and the edge stands. The check walks UP from the caller, so a sibling closure calling its parent's helper resolves too. Re-measured on the same three repos at the same shas: closure misses 60 -> 3 (requests 2->1, click 8->2, rich 50->0), and rich's overall recall 90% -> 98% with Tree.__rich_console__ -> make_guide now present. Rules 2 and 3 were NOT touched, as the diagnosis insisted: the 111 attribute-call refusals are the 0.54.3 fix working, and loosening them would trade a small under-report for the 369-edge hairball. THE REMAINING 3 ARE A DIFFERENT DEFECT, filed not fixed: where a def has @overload stubs, the parser emits src_qualname WITHOUT the #N disambiguator (raw edge reads 'src.requests.models.Response.iter_content'), so the call is attributed to the first stub while the nested helper is parented to iter_content#3. The scope check then correctly says the stub does not contain it. Same shape as the Java arity suffix: one name, two representations, emitter and registry unable to meet. PINNED IN TWO LAYERS because one was demonstrably not enough - every fixture in the suite passed while this bug shipped, since none had the caller be the encloser. Fast fixture in test_units_core2 (falsified both ways: revert the scope check, and remove guard 1 entirely), corpus floors in test_corpus_recall under 'pytest -m network'.

author: agent
text:
DEFECT, found by a human looking at the rendered map on 2026-08-18 and measured on prometheus/prometheus@6063ce7. A LANGUAGE BUILTIN IS BEING RESOLVED TO A REPO METHOD, at full confidence.

tsdb/head.go declares `func (c *memChunk) len() int`. It is the only entity in the repo whose short name is `len`, so candidates("len") returns exactly one, resolution is "exact", and EVERY `len(x)` in prometheus lands on it:

  tsdb.head.memChunk.len          1,619 incoming call edges
  next highest in the whole map     342

1,619 of 16,346 call edges - 9.9% of the map's call traffic - point at one 3-line method it has nothing to do with. Uniqueness was read as certainty, which is the same mistake 0.54.3 fixed for ambiguous names, arriving from the other direction: no competition looked like confidence when it is the case that most deserves suspicion.

THE RULE THAT WOULD FIX IT is already here in mirror image. Rule 2 says an ATTRIBUTE call cannot be a module-level function - `d.get(x)` is not `def get`. The converse is just as true: a BARE call cannot be a METHOD. `len(x)` is written with no receiver, and `memChunk.len` cannot be reached without one, however unique the name.

DO NOT IMPLEMENT IT YET, and this is the load-bearing part. via_attr is populated by the PYTHON PARSER ONLY (parsers.py, PythonParser). GoParser, JavaParser and the JS/TS parsers never set it, so every one of their calls arrives via_attr=False. A rule reading "bare call, therefore not a method" would treat EVERY Go and Java call as bare and refuse every method target - deleting the 3,150 gson method-to-method edges 0.56.0 existed to create. The rule is right and the data is not there to support it in four of five languages.

So the honest order is: teach the tree-sitter parsers to record via_attr (they already walk the call node and can see whether the function expression is a selector/field access), pin that each parser sets it, and only then add the mirror rule. Doing the rule first turns a 10% false-edge problem into a total loss of polyglot method resolution.

SCOPE. This is not only builtins. The same shape appears below `len` in the same map: DirLocker.Lock takes 342 edges, and `mu.Lock()` on a stdlib sync.Mutex is the obvious source; Timer.Duration takes 211. The general class is a call whose real target is OUTSIDE the repo - builtin, stdlib, or dependency - being attributed to a same-named entity inside it. Builtins are the tractable head of that distribution because the set is finite and defined by the language spec.

Not fixed as of 0.57.2. Recorded here because the reasoning for NOT fixing it in the obvious way is the part that would be lost.

author: agent
text:
SUPERSEDES the DEFECT note below. Fixed in 0.57.2; read that note for the measurements, not for what this code does.

WHAT SHIPPED, and it is narrower than the note below proposed. Rule 2b refuses a call only when the callee is a METHOD, the call site wrote NO receiver, and the name is one the CALLER'S LANGUAGE defines. prometheus: memChunk.len went 1,619 incoming call edges to 13, and the 13 are real - `chk.len()` with a receiver, one of which sits on the same line as a builtin call (`removedInOrder = chk.len() + len(s.mmappedChunks)`), which is now the Go fixture. gson holds at exactly 3,150 method-to-method edges, the number 0.56.0 built.

THE BROAD RULE THE NOTE BELOW PROPOSED IS FALSE, and this is the part worth keeping. "A bare call cannot be a method" is not true of Python: rich binds `add_row = items_table.add_row` and then calls `add_row(...)`. A bound-method alias keeps the name, so the reference really is that method, reached with no receiver. JS destructuring does the same. Implemented as stated, the rule cost rich 96% -> 94% and sqlalchemy its floor, in the first network run after the change. The corpus floors caught it; no fixture did, and no fixture would have - this is CLAUDE.md lesson 5 paying for itself.

Restricted to names the language itself defines, the claim is true again and still covers all of the measured harm, because the harm was builtins colliding with same-named methods.

TWO PIECES OF DATA HAD TO EXIST FIRST, both easy to get wrong:

1. via_attr was populated by the PYTHON PARSER ALONE. Go, Java and JS/TS never set it, so their calls all arrived looking receiverless. Adding any bare-call rule before fixing that would have refused every polyglot method target.

2. via_attr CANNOT ANSWER "was a receiver written". Python clears it when dst_override resolves an imported receiver - via_attr means "attribute call the parser could not resolve to a module". Reusing it as the bare-call signal refused every resolved-receiver call to a method. RawEdge.bare is a separate field for exactly this reason, and the two must not be merged again.

PARSE_SCHEMA_VERSION went 7 -> 10 across this work, one bump per field or semantic change: 8 for via_attr on the tree-sitter parsers, 9 for RawEdge.bare, 10 for builtin_names and the narrowed rule. Each was necessary - a cache warmed at the previous version replays edges missing the new field, which silently disables the rule rather than failing.

STILL OPEN, and unchanged by this: a call whose real target is outside the repo but is NOT a builtin. DirLocker.Lock still takes 342 edges on prometheus (`mu.Lock()` on a stdlib sync.Mutex) and Timer.Duration 211. Builtins were the tractable head of that distribution because the set is finite and the language defines it; stdlib and dependency receivers need type information the map does not have.
